description: Sacramentum

description: Ascension Day

name: null
description: Sunday and Monday after the birth of St Mary. Mentioned by the town chronicler in 1465 to have been the new fair among the three fairs in the town
Three-day fair on St Hubert

Autumn fair, which took place on seven days before St Willehad (8 November), according to a 1035 privilege. In 1288 it took place on the Birth of the Virgin Mary. The 1339 privilege for retail traders ('krämer') mentions the eight days after the Nativity of the Virgin Mary.

name: null
description: In 1382, the Autumn fair is mentioned to take place in the week after St Dionysius.
Horse and cattle fair, which is held once a year on the square known as Pferdemarkt (horse market) since 1491. It was cancelled at a later date and revived in 1715.
The horse fair started eight days before St James. The market right started four days earlier.
A (horse) fair on Sunday after St John's day was privileged in 1549.

A second cattle market on St Bartholomew was privileged in 1625. In the first hour of the market, only the duke was allowed to trade, in the second hour only Friedland citizens. Afterwards the market was free.
Fair on Sunday before St Simon and Jude

name: Oulu fair
description: Saloinen (Raahe) St Olaf’s (29 July) fair was relocated to Oulu in 1642 and set to St Laurentius (10 August), which may also have been an older date of fairs in Oulu rivermouth. The fair was confirmed to last eight days in 1650 and lengthened to twelve days in 1652.

name: Winter fair
description: Tammerkoski winter fair was ordained to be held for three days on St. Matthew (24 February) in 1638, but transferred to Epiphany (6 January) in 1639. The fair was relocated in 1708 to Harju and in 1750 to Pispala.

name: Tammerkoski autumn fair
description: Tammerkoski autumn fair was ordained to be held for three days on St Bartholomew (24 August). The fair was relocated in 1708 to Harju and in 1750 to Pispala.
The fair on St Walpurga was one of the original three fairs in Römhild, which date was moved in 1498. It is unknown how old it was.
Carnival fair, granted in 1498

name: Harju winter fair
description: Burghers of Pori were granted the rights of annual Candlemas winter fair in Harju in 1602 and again in 1604. The actual status of the fair since the 1610s is unknown. The fair was relocated in 1638 to Tammerkoski village.
Fair on Friday before St Martin.
Fair on Sunday after Corpus Christi

name: Brüdermarkt/Brüderablass
description: Fair connected to the church dedication festival on Ascension Day. Only locals are allowed to trade at first, in 1532 trade by non-locals is allowed.

name: Kemi Haminasaari
description: In 1622 the annual winter and summer fair in Kemi was set to New Year’s day (1 January) and St John the Baptist (24 June). In 1660 annual fairs were held in summer starting from the feast of apostle Peter (29 June) for 14 days.

name: Kemi Haminasaari winter fair
description: In 1622 the annual winter and summer fair in Kemi was set to New Year’s day (1 January) and St John the Baptist (24 June). In 1660 annual fairs were held in summer starting from the feast of apostle Peter (29 June) for 14 days.

name: Paltaniemi fair
description: The burghers of Oulu were granted the right of two annual fairs in Kajaneborg parish in 1625. Of these the summer fair was to be held at midsummer (24 June) in Paltaniemi. The fair was relocated to Kajaani in 1650.
Eight-day fair on the eve of St Mary Magdalene (21 July)

name: Kokkola fair
description: The annual fair in Kokkola was in 1642 ordained to be held on St Bartholomeus (24 August), in 1650 on St Olaf (29 July) and in 1652 again on St Bartholomeus.
Fair on St Bartholomew's day

name: Uusikaarlepyy fair
description: The annual St Olaf summer fair (29 July) in Pedersöre was transferred to Nykarleby in 1624 and ordered to last for three days

name: Vaasa winter fair
description: In the privileges of 1606 and 1611 Vaasa was confirmed two annual fairs, one on Candlemas (2 February) and one St Laurentius (10 August). The early autumn fair of St Laurentius was confirmed also in 1640 and is cited in 1708. Both fairs may date to the late 14th century.

name: Pedersöre St Olaf's fair
description: In 1616 burghers of Stockholm, Turku, Rauma and Pori were granted the right for annual fair of two weeks in Pedersöre and Saloinen starting from St Olaf’s (29 July). In 1624 Pedersöre the fair was transferred to Nykarleby and set to last for three days.

name: Bamismarkt
description: Fair on St. Bavo (1 October), with a duration of c. six weeks.
The cloth fair on St. James' Day lasted three days. The market right lasted a day longer. It has been moved to Petri ad Cathedram in an unknown year.
Fair on Monday after Judica
A fair on Sunday Cantate was granted in 1479.
Fair on Monday after Letare.
Fair on Peter and Paul's Day, granted in 1498.

name: Vaasa summer fair
description: In the privileges of 1606 and 1611 Vaasa was confirmed two annual fairs, one on Candlemas (2 February) and one St Laurentius (10 August). The early autumn fair of St Laurentius was confirmed also in 1640 and is cited in 1708. Both fairs may date to the late 14th century.

name: Pyhtää Church fair
description: St Laurentius (10 August) fair at Pyhtää Church is cited in 1584 when they were frequented by Helsinki burghers.

name: Korkeakoski fair
description: St Laurentius (10 August) Fair at Korkeakoski is cited in 1600 and 1606.

name: Kalajoki winter fair
description: The rights for Kalajoki winter fair on St Henrik (20.1.) were transferred to the new town of Kokkola (Karleby) in 1621. In 1622 the king granted the burghers of Kokkola and Oulu the right to trade in Kalajoki fairs on 18 May (feast of St Erik) and Laurentius (10.8.).
Fair during the rogation days.
Fair on St. Gall's day (16 October).

name: Halikko Fair
description: The medieval St Bridget (7 October) local peasant fair at Halikko church was relocated to Salo bridge some time in the early modern era.

name: Salo Bartholomeus fair
description: The known dates of Salo fairs in the 17th century are Apostle Bartolomeus (24 August) and Apostle Matteus (21 September) together with St Bridget (7 October) and a local peasant fair on the Assumption of Mary (15 August).
Fair held on St. Kilian's day (8 July). Its date changed slightly over the years. It could have lasted until St. Margaret's (22 July).
Market on Saturday before St John's day, founded in 1575.

name: Tornio summer fair
description: The summer fair in Tornio started in the Middle Ages and in 1519 at Midsummer (24 June). In 1649 the town applied the relocation of the fair to start on the eight day before midsummer.

name: Pori Fair
description: Pori was in 1602 and 1604 granted rights to three annual fairs, one of which took place in the town on apostle Bartolomeus (24 August) and is cited in almanacks in 1585 and 1598.

name: Lammainen fair
description: Pori was in 1602 and 1604 granted rights to three annual fairs, one of which took place in the town on apostle Bartolomeus (24 August). The other two fairs took place in Pirkkala in Harju at Candlemas (2 February) and on St Laurentius (10.8.) in Ulvila (Nakkila) Lammainen (some 25 kms upstream from Pori and 20 kms downstream from Kokemäki).

name: Rauma winter fair
description: Rauma annual winter fair on Candlemas (2 February) is cited in 1585 and 1598 and was confirmed in 1607. In 1624 the day was changed to Conversion of St Paul (25 January).

name: Männäinen Fair
description: Männäinen annual summer fair was in 1616 held on St Olaf (29 July).
Fair on Thursday after Easter.

name: Mynämäki winter fair
description: Mynämäki annual winter fair was in 1623 held on Candlemas (2 February).

name: Uusikaupunki winter fair
description: Uusikaupunki annual winter fair was in 1625–89 held on the second Sunday of Lent (15 February - 21 March).

name: Naantali winter fair
description: The annual winter fair on Ash Wednesday (4 February–10 March) in Naantali is mentioned in 1506, but they were possibly held as early as 1452. During the reign of Queen Christina (1632–54), the burghers of Naantali applied to have St Bridget (7 October) to be set as an annual fair day with Ash Wednesday, which may hint about St Bridget fairs medieval origins. The request was granted in 1660, when the autumn fair was set to Michaelmas (29 September).

name: Inkoo fair
description: Burghers of Helsinki were in 1594 granted rights to annual apostle Matteus (21 September) fair in Inkoo. In 1614, the burghers of Tammisaari (sw. Ekenäs) tried unsuccessfully to relocate the fair in their town.
Fair eight days before St. Martin's day.

name: Lohja Candlemas Fair
description: Lohja Candlemas fair (2 February) is mentioned in 1592, 1618, 1627 and 1650. The fair was translocated together with Saturday before Mid-Lent fair (28/29 February – 3 April) to Tammisaari, from where they were moved back before 1634.

name: Perniö fair
description: The earliest record of the Perniö Laurentius (10.8.) fair is from 1599, but since Apostle Laurentius is cited as the patron saint of Perniö stone church built in 1460–80 it is of medieval origin.
Eight-day fair on the Feast of the eleven thousand Virgins (21 October).
Pentecost fair with a duration of c. six weeks.
Cattle and free fair on Saturday after St Lawrence.
Fair on Sunday before St Burkhard's day, granted in 1498.

name: Kajaani summer fair
description: Paltaniemi midsummer fair was relocated to Kajaani in 1650.

name: Kristiinankaupunki autumn fair
description: In 1650-51 two annual fairs were confirmed for Kristiinankaupunki; one at the elevation of Holy Cross (14 September) and the other at Candlemas (2 February).

name: Kristiinankaupunki winter fair
description: In 1650-51 two annual fairs were confirmed for Kristiinankaupunki; one at the elevation of Holy Cross (14 September) and the other at Candlemas (2 February).
Fair on All Saints Day.
Fair on Sunday after the Assumption of Mary.
Fair on St Gall

name: Porvoo autumn fair
description: The earliest information on annual fairs in Porvoo are from the year 1584 when king Johan III confirmed the town its two traditional fairs on Visitation of Mary (2 July, apparently in Saksala) and Exaltation of the Holy Cross (14 September, in town). The latter fair is cited in almanacs in 1598. Both days were again confirmed in 1594. In 1650 an annual winter fair in Porvoo was confirmed to be hold at Epiphany (6 January).

name: Vöyri summer fair
description: In 1622 Vöyri had two annual fairs on St Margaret (20 July) and St Mary (8 September?). In 1650 burghers of Nykarleby were further granted sole right to hold a local fair for four days starting on St Nicolaus (6 December) in Vöyri.
Fair on the Nativity of Mary, with a duration of eight days before and 15 days after the feast day.
Fair on the Nativity of St John the Baptist, with a duration of eight days.

name: Isokyrö winter fair
description: In 1622 Isokyrö fairs were held on the feast of St Henrik (of Finland, 20 January) in winter and St Laurentius (10 August) in late summer, both dates of which may go back to the Middle Ages.

name: Isokyrö autumn fair
description: In 1622 Isokyrö fairs were held on the feast of St Henrik (of Finland, 20 January) in winter and St Laurentius (10 August) in late summer, both dates of which may go back to the Middle Ages.

name: Lapua winter fair
description: Lapua fair was in 1622 held on Candlemas (2 February). Another fair was in the early 17th century held at Michaelmas (29 September).

name: Pernaja autumn fair
description: Pernaja fair was in 1584 held on Michaelmas (29 September).

name: Pyhtää Vähä-Ahvenkoski fair
description: Pyhtää fair is first cited in 1553. In 1584 the St Bartholomeus (24 August) fair was very likely held at Vähä-Ahvenkoski fair site which remained in use to the 19th century. Information also exists on St Laurentius (10 August) fair at Pyhtää church.

name: Sipoo midsummer fair
description: Sipoo Midsummer fair (24 June) is first cited in 1576. The fair was relocated in Helsinki in 1584. The burghers of Helsinki also had rights over an autumn fair in Sipoo on St Mary (8 September) as early as 1616. The duration of the fair was in 1682 confirmed to two days.
Fair on St Bartholomew's Day, probably going back to the dedication of the local church.

name: Helsinki summer fair
description: When king Johan III in 1584 ordained the midsummer fair (24 June) at Sipoo (sw. Sibbo) to be relocated to Helsinki, he also confirmed a winter fair to be held on Epiphany (6 January). Both fairs were continued in the new town in the 1640s. In the 1650s the burghers applied the date of the winter fair to be changed first to Candlemas (2 February) and to Apostle Paul (25 January) in 1680.

name: Helsinki summer fair
description: When king Johan III in 1584 ordained the midsummer fair (24 June) at Sipoo (sw. Sibbo) to be relocated to Helsinki, he also confirmed a winter fair to be held on Epiphany (6 January). Both fairs were continued in the new town in the 1640s.

name: Salo Matteus Fair
description: The known dates of Salo fairs in the 17th century are Apostle Bartolomeus (24 August) and Apostle Matteus (21 September) together with St Bridget (7 October) and a local peasant fair on the Assumption of Mary (15 August).

name: Kalajoki spring fair
description: In 1622 the king granted the burghers of Kokkola and Oulu the right to trade in Kalajoki fairs on 18 May (feast of St Erik) and Laurentius (10.8.).

name: Rauma winter fair 1624
description: Rauma annual winter fair on Candlemas (2 February) is cited in 1585 and 1598 and was confirmed in 1607. In 1624 the day was changed to Conversion of St Paul (25 January).
Fair on the first working day after St Martin (11 November).

name: Mynämäki autumn fair
description: Mynämäki annual autumn fair was in 1623 held on St Laurentius (10 August).

name: Uusikaupunki autumn fair
description: Uusikaupunki annual autumn fair was in 1623–1654 held on St Laurentius (10 August).

name: null
description: Fair on St Dionysius.
Cattle and free fair on Monday after St Lawrence

name: Kajaani winter fair
description: Kajaani annual winter fair was ordained in 1650 to be held on Candlemas (2 February).
Fair on St James's Day
Fair on Sunday after the Assumption of Mary is moved to Sunday after All Saint's Day, because the original fair took place during harvest time.

name: null
description: An annual midsummer fair, which probably took place June 21. Held at Thisted from 1547 to 1573 when it was moved back to Vestervig.

name: null
description: A Pentecost market is mentioned in 1559.

The latter fair is cited in almanacs in 1598. Both days were again confirmed in 1594. In 1650 an annual winter fair in Porvoo was confirmed to be hold at Epiphany (6 January).
Fair on the Nativity of Mary, with a duration of eight days.

name: Lapua autumn fair
description: Lapua fair was in 1622 held on Candlemas (2 February). Another fair was in the early 17th century held at Michaelmas (29 September).

name: Sipoo autumn fair
description: Sipoo Midsummer fair (24 June) is first cited in 1576. The fair was relocated in Helsinki in 1584. The burghers of Helsinki also had rights over an autumn fair in Sipoo on St Mary (8 September) as early as 1616. The duration of the fair was in 1682 confirmed to two days.

name: Helsinki winter fair
description: When king Johan III in 1584 ordained the midsummer fair (24 June) at Sipoo (sw. Sibbo) to be relocated to Helsinki, he also confirmed a winter fair to be held on Epiphany (6 January). Both fairs were continued in the new town in the 1640s. In the 1650s the burghers applied the date of the winter fair to be changed first to Candlemas (2 February) and to Apostle Paul (25 January) in 1680.

name: Helsinki winter fair
description: When king Johan III in 1584 ordained the midsummer fair (24 June) at Sipoo (sw. Sibbo) to be relocated to Helsinki, he also confirmed a winter fair to be held on Epiphany (6 January). Both fairs were continued in the new town in the 1640s.

name: Salo St Bridget Fair
description: The known dates of Salo fairs in the 17th century are Apostle Bartolomeus (24 August) and Apostle Matteus (21 September) together with St Bridget (7 October) and a local peasant fair on the Assumption of Mary (15 August).

name: Kalajoki autumn fair
description: In 1622 the king granted the burghers of Kokkola and Oulu the right to trade in Kalajoki fairs on 18 May (feast of St Erik) and Laurentius (10.8.).

name: Rauma summer fair
description: Rauma summer fair was in 1607 confirmed to be held on Midsummer (24 June). In 1624 the annual fair was changed to St Bartholomeus (24 August).

name: Paimio Fair
description: Paimio St James Fair (25 July) is cited in 1672 when the burghers of Turku applied for their closure. Very likely a local peasant fair of medieval origin, the fair was held near to the old (pre 1680s) site of the parish church.
Lohja Saturday before Mid-Lent fair (28/29 February – 3 April) is cited in 1627.

name: Vöyri autumn fair
description: In 1622 Vöyri had two annual fairs on St Margaret (20 July) and St Mary (8 September?). In 1650 burghers of Nykarleby were further granted sole right to hold a local fair for four days starting on St Nicolaus (6 December) in Vöyri.

name: Salo Assumption of Mary Fair
description: The known dates of Salo fairs in the 17th century are Apostle Bartolomeus (24 August) and Apostle Matteus (21 September) together with St Bridget (7 October) and a local peasant fair on the Assumption of Mary (15 August).

name: Rauuma autumn fair
description: Rauma summer fair was in 1607 confirmed to be held on Midsummer (24 June). In 1624 the annual fair was changed to St Bartholomeus (24 August).

name: Jääski fair
description: Apostle Peter’s (29 June) annual fair in Jääski was confirmed in 1542 and 1594.

name: Karjalohja winter fair
description: Karjalohja's fair was held in 1627 on the feast of Apostle Paul (25 January).

name: Tammisaari winter fair
description: In 1627, Lohja Candlemas (2 February) and Saturday before Mid-Lent Sunday (28/29 February – 3 April) fairs were moved together with the Apostle Paul's (25 January) fair of Karjalohja to Tammisaari to be held as a single Candlemas (2 February) fair in the town. The fairs were returned to Lohja and Karjalohja before 1634.
Annual fair on the elevation of the Holy Cross (14 September) in Äyräpää was confirmed in 1542 and 1594. The rights of burghers of Viborg to annual fair in Muolaa was confirmed in 1627.

name: Vehkalahti Sf Olaf's fair
description: Burghers of Viborg were in 1542 granted sole right for annual fair in Vehkalahti on St Olaf’s (29 July). In 1585 the fair was held on apostle Bartholomeus (24 August). In 1594 the fair day was confirmed as St Laurentius (10 August).
Fair on St Servatius (13 May), with a duration of eight days before and after that date.
Fair on St Remigius (1 October), with a duration of eight days before and after that date

name: Lapvesi Nativity of Mary fair
description: Burghers of Viborg were in 1542 granted sole right for an annual fair in Lapvesi on the Nativity of Mary (8 September). The right was confirmed in 1594. In 1621 the fair was confirmed to last one week.

name: Saksala fair
description: The Visitation of Mary fair (2 July) confirmed for Porvoo in 1584 appears to have been traditionally organised in Saksala. In 1616 the tar fair organised by burghers of Helsinki in Porvoo area on 1 July was called St Enewald’s fair, which may echo a 15th century date for the summer fair in Porvoonjoki area. Local fairs were organised in Saksala as late as in the early 19th century.
Viipuri was in 1647 granted an annual cattle fair to be held on St Bartholomeus (24 August), but its popularity remained low.

name: Häömeenlinnan winter fair
description: Hämeenlinna was in 1650 confirmed two annual fairs on Epiphany (6 January), and 1 September, of which the latter was in the same year changed to St Olaf (29 July).

name: Saaresmäki
description: The burghers of Oulu were granted the right of two annual fairs in Kajaneborg parish in 1625. Of these the summer fair was to be held at midsummer (24 June) in Paltaniemi and the winter fair on 15 December in Saaresmäki (Särismäki). It is unknown if the Saaresmäki fair took place.
Fair on the Birth of St Mary, mentioned in 1417 as already in existence
Fair on St. Michael's day

name: Savonlinna summer fair
description: In 1643 an annual fair was proposed to be established on the day of the Apostles St. Peter and St Paul (29 June) in Savonlinna.

name: Turkhauta fair
description: The burghers of Helsinki were in 1614 granted the sole right to the annual fair market held in Turkhauta in Janakkala on 1 September. In 1654, the fair day was changed to 14 September.

name: Bobäck  fair
description: The burghers of Helsinki were in 1584 granted the rights for an annual fair in Kirkkonummi Bobäck on Michaelmas (29 September). The rights were confirmed in 1594 when the date was cited as the Nativity of St Mary (8 September) and the site as Brendeberg’s sund.

name: Saloinen fair
description: The oldest site for the annual fair was in Satamalahti and after that in Markkinaniemi in Satamakangas, where the fair may have been relocated in 1420. St Olaf’s (29 July) fair in Saloinen is cited in 1616, but was relocated in 1642 to Oulu and set to St Laurentius (10 August). A smaller annual fair designed for local peasants was allowed in Saloinen whatever day they saw the best.

name: Tuiku winter fair
description: Turku annual Winter fair on the feast of St Henrik (20 January) is documented in 1531 but has a 14th century origin.
On 4 June 1303 count John granted a fair on the eve of St Margaret (July 12). The fair must have decayed later, because it was re-installed by archduke Philip with a duration of 8 days in 1497.
Fair on the day of the Holy Cross (14 September), the consecration day of St. Peter's church. The burgrave levied a toll on the fair, which is first mentioned around 1360.
Horse fair on Saint Michael (29 September), which might also have been held in May in the beginning. It was moved to Saint Matthew in 1633.

name: Vöyri winter fair
description: In 1622 Vöyri had two annual fairs on St Margaret (20 July) and St Mary (8 September?). In 1650 burghers of Nykarleby were further granted sole right to hold a local fair for four days starting on St Nicolaus (6 December) in Vöyri.

name: VEhkalahti St Bartholomeus fair
description: Burghers of Viborg were in 1542 granted sole right for annual fair in Vehkalahti on St Olaf’s (29 July). In 1585 the fair was held on apostle Bartholomeus (24 August). In 1594 the fair day was confirmed as St Laurentius (10 August).
Fair on St Remaclus (3 September), with a duration of eight days before and after that date.

name: Lapvesi Michaelmas fair
description: Burghers of Viborg were in 1621 granted further two weeks annual fair in Lapvesi to start on Michaelmas (29 September).

name: Hämeenlinna summer fair
description: Hämeenlinna was in 1650 confirmed two annual fairs on Epiphany (6 January), and 1 September, of which the latter was in the same year changed to St Olaf (29 July).

Fair from two days before until two days after St Ulrich's day (4 July, the dedication day of St. Patrokli church), as mentioned in 1417. According to a complaint from 1504, it attracted visitors from the territories of Cologne, Utrecht, Münster, Osnabrück, Paderborn, Cleves, Mark, Berg, Hesse, Lippe and Rietberg.
Fair on mid-Lent

name: Turku Summer fair
description: Turku annual Summer fair on the translation of St Henrik (18 June) is documented in 1531 but has a 14th century origin.

name: Vehkalahti St Laurentius fair
description: Burghers of Viborg were in 1542 granted sole right for annual fair in Vehkalahti on St Olaf’s (29 July). In 1585 the fair was held on apostle Bartholomeus (24 August). In 1594 the fair day was confirmed as St Laurentius (10 August).
Fair from three days before until three days after All Saints, as mentioned in 1417. It continues to exist today as a fun fair.
Fair on Sunday after St. Kilian's day

name: Turku Autumn fair
description: Turku annual Autumn free fair was ordained in 1636 to start on the Nativity of Mary and last for two weeks.

name: Æbelholt
description: The annual fair of the monastery of Æbelholt is first mentioned in 1265, but is probably older. The fair took place from June 15th to June 29th, and at least in the high middle ages horses were the most important commodity. In 1562 the fair was removed to Frederiksborg.

name: Saint Kjeld’s
description: Presumably, the oldest fair was Saint Kjeld’s fair (Danish: Sankt Kjeldsmarked), which is first mentioned in the town law from 1440, but apparently began in the high medieval period. Saint Kjeld’s fair was held July 11th in the 15th century.

name: null
description: During the 1400ties Saint Kjeld’s fair was repressed by the Saint Mauritii’s fair (Danish: Sankt Maurutti marked/Toftemarkedet), which was held September 22th to September 24th.

name: null
description: The fair of St Michael was shortened to three days between 1488 and 1523.

name: Snapstinget
description: The most important annual fair in Viborg during the late medieval period and early-modern era was ‘Snapstinget’. This is mentioned for the first time in 1442, where it was held on the day of Saint Canute (Danish: Sankt Knuds dag), i.e. January 6th, but the market activity in January may very well be older.

name: Snapstinget
description: Around the middle of the 15th century the opening of the fair was removed to the first Saturday after Epiphany. Hereby ‘Snapstinget’ followed immediately after ‘Kieler Umschlag' in the town of Kiel in Holstein, which was held annually January 6th to January 13th, and clearly there was a connection between the two capital markets. ‘Snapstinget’ continued as one of the most important annual faris in Denmark up until the modern era.

name: Glenstrup
description: The fair at the village of Glenstrup was relocated to Hobro in 1552.

name: Dybdal
description: in 1561 the markets previously held in Dybdal and Testrup were moved to Hobro. This resulted in dissatisfaction among the local peasantry, and in 1578 one of the fairs was moved back to Testrup.

name: Testrup
description: in 1561 the markets previously held in Dybdal and Testrup were moved to Hobro. This resulted in dissatisfaction among the local peasantry, and in 1578 one of the fairs was moved back to Testrup.

description: Fair on St Peter and Paul's day, which is first explicitly mentioned in 1305, but probably went back to the early days of the town in the 11th century. It was the most important fair in Naumburg and acquired interregional significance in the 15th century. It survived the conflicts with Leipzig in the 16th century, although it was located within the exclusive 15 miles zone around Leipzig, making it effectively one of the four fairs in the Leipzig cycle.

description: Countess Margareta of Flanders granted Aardenburg the right to hold a fair on the 14 days following Trinity Sunday in 1268. The privilege was confirmed in 1299, then it consisted off three days a horsemarket and three days a clothmarket. By 1423, the market still existed but had lost all significance. Duke Philip the Good tried to revive it, but it must have disappeared soon after. Emperor Charles V tried this again, he reconfirmed the fair of 1268 and installed in 1521 a second fair three days after St. Lukesday (Oct. 18.), again without success.

description: The fair of Saint Canute (Danish: Sankt Knudmesse marked) held the days immediately before and after the 10th of July. The fair was made the only legal fair on the island of Funen in 1540. At least in the 17th century and probably also before the fair had a regional character and drew visitors from Copenhagen, Ribe and Flensburg.

name: Sankt Hans marked
description: Saint John’s fair (Danish: Sankt Hans marked) on the 24th June. First mentioned in 1252, but probably older. Originally, one of the most important commodities at this summer fair appears to have been stockfish. In the later middle ages the fair lost importance to the other annual fairs in Ribe.

name: Vor Frue marked
description: The fair of Our Lady (Danish: Vor Frue marked or Ribemarket) began on the 8th of September, and according to privileges from 1494, the fair lasted five days. The fair was well established prior to 1410, and was probably mentioned for the first time in 1384. The fair was, however, most likely older. The main commodity was oxen and the fair attracted traders from both Denmark and foreign regions, in particular different parts of northwestern Europe. During the 15th century several thousand of oxen were bought at The fair of Our Lady each year. Most of the was exported to Flanders and Northern Germany.

name: Spring Fair
description: A fair during spring, which began on the day of Our Lady Annunciation (i.e. March 25th). First mentioned in 1485 but probably older. Oxen was the main commodity.

name: Saint Knud’s fair.

name: Ascension fair
description: In 1561 a fair previously held at Alhede (two miles from Hjørring) on the 24th august was joined with the Ascension fair in 1561. The latter was maybe already held in Hjørring. The newly established fair was held on the eight day after the feast of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle (August 24th), i.e. September 1th.

name: Midfaste marked
description: An annual fair was held at Laetare Sunday (Danish: Midfaste markedet). The fair was first mentioned in 1345, but is most likely to be older. The most important commodities were oxen and horses. In 1603 king Christian IV (1588-1648) moved the fair to February 3

name: Sankt Hans marked
description: Another annual fair was held around the feast of John the Baptist (Danish: Sankt Hans marked), either in the end of June or early in July. Originally the opening day of the fair was June 24th. The fair ran for three days. The fair was probably etablished in the late medieval period, but this is not certain.

A new Pentecost fair in Nibe was established in 1590 but it was prohibited in 1594.

name: Saint Francis fair
description: Saint Francis fair on the feast of Saint Francis (October 4th). One of the most important annual fairs in Denmark. In the year 1491 about 4000 oxen from the fair in Kolding were exported to Germany via the toll station at Gottorp. The fair lasted three days.
